# Inference benchmark notes

Date: 2026-08-25. Fixed trained checkpoints:
runs/plain_40k.fblt (plain BLT, 1.26-1.43 held-out BPB) and
runs/bltd_l03_40k.fblt (BLT-D lambda<=0.3, 1.65-1.99 BPB).
Driver: bin/infer_bench (make bench-infer); data: 8 held-out prompts
(64-byte, deep offsets) x 64 new bytes each; results in
bench/results.jsonl (experiment group "6_infer"); charts in runs/bench_graphs/
(rendered by tools/bench_plots.py).

## Results (aggregated over 512 generated bytes per config)

dec/byte = decoder forward passes per generated byte;
enc/byte = encoder+global passes per byte; acc = drafted-byte
acceptance; agree = fraction of new bytes equal to the same model's
greedy output.

| Config            | dec/byte | enc/byte | acc   | agree |
|-------------------|---------:|---------:|------:|------:|
| plain greedy      | 1.00     | 1.00     | —     | 1.00  |
| plain BLT-S k=4   | 1.17     | 0.48     | 0.82  | 1.00  |
| plain BLT-S k=8   | 1.26     | 0.29     | 0.77  | 1.00  |
| plain BLT-S k=16  | 1.61     | 0.21     | 0.59  | 1.00  |
| bltd greedy       | 1.00     | 1.00     | —     | 1.00  |
| bltd BLT-S k=4    | 1.45     | 0.59     | 0.61  | 1.00  |
| bltd BLT-S k=8    | 2.16     | 0.50     | 0.39  | 1.00  |
| bltd BLT-S k=16   | 3.69     | 0.48     | 0.22  | 1.00  |
| bltd BLT-D B=4    | 0.29     | 0.25     | n/a   | 0.08  |
| bltd BLT-D B=8    | 0.17     | 0.13     | n/a   | 0.14  |
| bltd BLT-D B=16   | 0.09     | 0.06     | n/a   | 0.12  |
| bltd BLT-D-EB B=8 | 0.16     | 0.13     | n/a   | 0.14  |
| bltd BLT-DV B=4   | 0.81     | 0.75     | 0.43  | 1.00  |
| bltd BLT-DV B=8   | 0.79     | 0.66     | 0.26  | 1.00  |
| bltd BLT-DV B=16  | 0.80     | 0.63     | 0.15  | 1.00  |
| bltd DV one-step  | 0.66     | 0.66     | 0.26  | 1.00  |
| bltd DV-EB g=1    | 0.79     | 0.67     | 0.26  | 1.00  |
| bltd DV-EB g=2    | 0.70     | 0.66     | 0.26  | 1.00  |

Wall-clock (informational; KV-cache use differs between paths):
plain BLT-S k=16 304 ms/prompt vs greedy 1554 ms (5.1x); raw BLT-D
B=16 116 ms (13x, quality-divergent); DV variants ~1030-1200 ms.

## Findings

1. **BLT-S is the toy-scale winner on well-trained causal models**:
   byte-identical output, 52-79% fewer encoder/global passes, 4-5x
   wall-clock. Matches the paper's claim (section 5.3) that BLT-S
   trades decoder NFEs for large enc/global savings with no quality loss.
2. **The diffusion tax shows up at inference too**: BLT-S acceptance on
   the BLT-D model (61/39/22%) is far below the plain model's
   (82/77/59%) because BLT-D's causal head is weaker (see
   training_notes.md).
3. **BLT-DV preserves quality exactly** (agreement 1.00 enforced by an
   in-bench assertion) while saving ~20-34% decoder NFEs and ~25-37%
   encoder passes at toy scale. One-step diffusion + verification is
   the best DV variant (dec 0.66/byte) -- consistent with the paper's
   "one-step + verify is fastest" finding.
4. **Raw BLT-D drafting is extremely cheap but diverges from greedy**
   (8-14% agreement): useful only where exact greedy parity is not
   required (e.g., diverse sampling with EB + top-p).
5. **Acceptance is bounded by the fully-masked (t~1) regime**: with
   lambda<=0.3 reweighting, L_mask is under-trained exactly where
   drafting starts (all-MASK blocks). This is the main lever for DV.

## Improvement directions (paper suggestions + my own)

Paper-sanctioned:
- Reweight toward next-byte prediction (section 6): done as lambda cap;
  next step is a SCHEDULE -- keep lambda low early, raise it late so the
  t~1 end gets dedicated capacity after the causal head stabilizes.
- Scale the decoder: BLT-D/DV savings are decoder-NFE savings; a bigger
  decoder makes them worth more (paper explicitly used a small decoder).
- One-step + verify as the default DV operating point.

My own:
- High-t curriculum: sample t ~ U(t_min, 1) with mass pushed toward 1
  late in training (directly targets drafting-from-scratch states).
- Train/infer patcher consistency: we trained with fixed-stride patches
  but generate with the entropy patcher; training BLT-D with the entropy
  patcher (or generating with the training patcher) should lift
  acceptance.
- Cache-aware diffusion drafting: the INFER mask keeps clean-row K/V
  stable across unmasking passes; reusing tier-1 KV for clean rows and
  recomputing only block rows would cut DV decoder cost further
  (block_generation currently runs dense passes).
- Hybrid scheduling: BLT-S for cheap enc/global amortization + DV-style
  verification of diffusion drafts within the same round.

## Reproduce

    make bench-infer
    python3 tools/bench_plots.py

## Follow-up improvement round (post-benchmarks, pre-CUDA)

Three ideas tested after the first benchmark pass; two rejected, one
kept. All numbers: same 8x64 protocol.

### 1. Fixed-stride-4 patching at inference (train/infer consistency)

Rationale: checkpoints were trained with fixed-4 patches; generating
with the entropy patcher mismatches. Result: REJECTED, with a structural
discovery -- fixed-4 breaks the DV == greedy invariant outright (commit
points land mid-patch; the final prefix latent absorbs draft bytes) and
does not improve acceptance (0.41/0.23/0.14 vs 0.43/0.26/0.15).

### 2. Verification boundary fix (KEPT)

Root-caused the equality condition: DV == greedy holds exactly only when
commit points coincide with patch boundaries. The original random-init
entropy LM produced 1-2 byte patches (boundary everywhere), masking the
issue; any real patcher exposes it. Fix applied to blt_verify_draft:
force a patch boundary at the commit point l before encoding the
candidate. Improves BLT-S agreement under a trained LM
(k=16: 0.746 -> 0.807) and is strictly more correct. Exact equality
remains unattainable with content-driven patching because greedy itself
re-segments at every commit; the bench gate is now agreement >= 0.90
(unit tests keep the exact gate under their controlled patcher).

### 3. Trained entropy LM + consistency retraining (REJECTED at this scale)

Trained the 1-layer entropy LM properly (runs/entlm.bin, CE ~2.7 nats)
and retrained BLT-D on its boundaries (32k steps). Training converged
far better than with the random LM (final loss 2.0 vs 4+; causal BPB
3.85 vs 9.64 in the matched regime), but generation got WORSE:
- BLT-S acceptance on bltd: 0.42/0.22/0.12 (vs 0.54/0.33/0.18)
- raw draft agreement: 0.03-0.04 (vs 0.09-0.14)
- DV draft agreement on prompt 0: 0.08
Content-driven variable-length patching makes the toy model's learning
problem harder (longer, irregular contexts) and verification noisier.
At 300k params the flexibility loss dominates the alignment gain.

Also tested and rejected: raising the L_mask weight late in training
(lambda 0.3 -> 1.0 over the last 8k steps). The mask gradient (weight up
to 1/t = 20 per cell) destabilizes the decayed final stretch; causal BPB went
1.65 -> 4.10. Retry only at larger scale with a gentler ramp.

### Settlement for the CUDA work

Keep the headline operating point: fixed-4-trained checkpoints +
the (random-init) entropy LM at inference -- degenerate 1-2 byte patches
give exact verification equivalence and the best acceptance. The
trained-LM infrastructure (blt_entropy_lm_save/load, --entropy-lm,
--train-entropy-lm) stays for future larger-scale runs where the paper's
patcher-consistency argument should win.
